# Incident Report: STRRAT Infection on DESKTOP-SKBR25F

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 585.7 sec, captured 2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34 UTC). No IDS/alert files were provided alongside the pcap; all findings below come directly from packet inspection with tshark.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 | Source of all C2 traffic; LAN is 172.16.1.0/24, gateway 172.16.1.1 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4`/`arp.src.hw_mac`) and Ethernet source on every frame from 172.16.1.66 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F | NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` registration, DNS self-registration to the DC, and literally embedded in the malware's own C2 beacon string |
| Logged-in user | ccollier | Kerberos `CNameString` from 172.16.1.66 to the DC (172.16.1.4), and embedded in the malware's C2 beacon string |
| Domain / DC | wiresharkworkshop.online, DC hostname WIRESHARK-WS-DC at 172.16.1.4 | LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos/DNS SRV records |

## Malware family

**STRRAT**, version **1.6**.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed at the protocol level** — this is not inferred from behavior or an external IDS rule. The malware's own C2 traffic is a semi-plaintext, pipe-delimited beacon that self-identifies:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Observed over TCP stream (tshark stream 83), source port 49754 → destination 141.98.10.79:12132, repeating on a fixed ~5-second interval for the remainder of the capture (first beacon at t=76.99s, last at t≈149.8s+, uptime counter climbing to "5 min 10 sec"). Fields decode as: literal string `STRRAT`, a client/campaign ID (`1BE8292C`), victim hostname, logged-on username, OS version, AV product (Windows Defender), a base64-encoded field that decodes to active-window/folder names (e.g. `Documents`, `Pictures`, `Home`, `Program Manager`) — consistent with STRRAT's known active-window-title polling behavior — malware version, geolocated country, and a "keylogger not installed" status flag.

Approximately 9 seconds before the first C2 beacon, the host resolved and connected to `github.com` (140.82.113.3), `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133), and `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209, an 8.8 MB transfer) in quick succession (t=63.96–68.0s). This sequence, immediately followed by malware execution and beaconing, is consistent with a staged download of the STRRAT loader/JAR and a Java runtime component, but all three of those sessions are TLS-encrypted (SNI only) — no cleartext URL, filename, or object was recoverable from this capture, so the exact delivery artifact is **not confirmed**, only correlated by timing.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` (TCP, plaintext STRRAT beacon protocol, no TLS) — confirmed malicious C2, sole C2 endpoint observed in this capture

**Malicious/suspicious domains and URLs**
- `ip-api.com` → `208.95.112.1`, plaintext HTTP `GET /json/` (User-Agent: `Chrome/73.0.3683.86`) at t=77.87s — IP geolocation/fingerprinting lookup, response confirmed the WAN IP `136.49.34.127` (Austin, TX, Google Fiber) and country `US`, matching the `US:United States` field the STRRAT beacon then reports. This is host reconnaissance by the malware, not a C2 channel — flagged as an IOC because of its role in the infection chain, not because ip-api.com itself is malicious infrastructure.

No malicious domain was observed for the C2 channel itself (141.98.10.79 was contacted directly by IP, no DNS lookup preceded it) — the bare-IP connection with no corresponding DNS query is itself a C2 tell.

**Benign context (not indicators)** — for completeness, ruled out as background noise: Microsoft/Office 365 telemetry and services (`*.msn.com`, `*.office.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, etc.), Bing, Skype, OneDrive/SFX, Windows NCSI (`www.msftconnecttest.com`), and Oracle Java auto-update (`javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com`, occurring at t=340s, well after infection and unrelated to it).

**Transferred files / hashes**
- No malware binary, JAR, or executable was recoverable from this capture. `tshark --export-objects` over HTTP yielded only two benign artifacts: `connecttest.txt` (Microsoft NCSI probe) and the `ip-api.com` JSON response. The suspected delivery downloads (github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, repo1.maven.org) were all TLS-encrypted, so **no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this evidence** — do not report a hash for this incident based on this pcap alone.

## Summary

DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user `ccollier` on the `wiresharkworkshop.online` domain, is infected with **STRRAT v1.6**. The malware performed an IP-geolocation/fingerprinting check against `ip-api.com` and then began persistent plaintext beaconing to its C2 at **141.98.10.79:12132**, self-reporting host details and polling active window/folder titles every ~5 seconds for the remainder of the capture. Attribution to STRRAT is confirmed directly from the malware's own C2 protocol strings, not inferred. The likely delivery vector involved near-simultaneous TLS sessions to github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, and repo1.maven.org immediately before infection, but this capture alone cannot confirm the delivered file or its hash due to TLS encryption.
